steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The crucifixion demonstrates the depth of God's love — God was willing to suffer the most painful and humiliating death to save humanity. Christians remember this through the symbol of the cross.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — The Crucifixion and Resurrection
steps.body: 1. For The Crucifixion and Resurrection questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of The Crucifixion and Resurrection to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain why the resurrection is important for Christians. | Q: Explain two ways the crucifixion is significant for Christians.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
